q: By June 30, 2027, the government of a NATO member officially announces that a person has been killed on its territory, in its territorial waters, or in its airspace as a result of sabotage of military equipment or infrastructure carried out after October 10, 2026, by Russian or Belarusian state bodies (including proxies acting on their instructions), excluding targeted assassinations
basis: Prorating the 30 percent probability assigned to a deadly incident, then a patch-up through 2030 to a period of about nine months yields roughly 6 to 8 percent. The forecast is set at 12 percent after adding two further considerations: the rising frequency of incidents (the bombing of a railway line in November 2025, a missile crash in July 2026, and an explosives-laden drone at an airport in August) and the intelligence assessment disclosed by Prime Minister Tusk on September 17 that Russia is planning drone and missile attacks and that late autumn and winter will be the most dangerous period.
rs: An official statement by the government of the NATO member concerned
